title: finding(devx): a Vite alias matches by PREFIX, so the dev server resolves package subpaths the `exports` map forbids — third resolver with this false green, and the repair coupled the console's type program to 30 workspace sources
body:
Filed by the `domain:ui` PM seat (`session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S`) from the PR #8668 CI repair. ⛔ Not claimed.

## The mechanism

A dev-only browser fixture in `apps/console` imported `@object-ui/app-shell/hooks/…` and `@object-ui/auth/AuthContext`. **Neither package publishes any subpath** — `.` is the whole of both `exports` maps.

> **A Vite string alias matches by PREFIX**, so the dev server resolved them and `tsc`, reading the `exports` map, did not.

⇒ the fixture ran correctly in the browser — **20/20 checks, twice** — and `Build Console` died with **six `TS2307`s**. The code was never importable; it merely appeared to be, in the one environment anybody looked at it in.

## ⭐ Third resolver, same false green

This repo already carries two measured instances of *"resolves a deep import the package's own `exports` map forbids"*:

- **vitest** — green under vitest, `TS2307` under `tsc`; measured three separate times and carried in every dispatch this session;
- **the wrong-cwd re-root** — `cd packages/X && pnpm exec vitest` silently re-rooting onto `apps/console` (objectui#3378's guard covers the `--filter` spelling).

**Vite's `resolve.alias` is the third**, and it is the one with the widest blast radius, because it is the resolver the **dev server** uses: anything a developer verifies by running the app can depend on a specifier the published package refuses. ⚠️ And unlike the vitest case, **no test needs to exist** for the divergence to bite — this fixture never runs under vitest at all.

⇒ the general statement, which is what makes this worth a card: **three independent resolvers in this repo answer "is this specifier importable?" differently from the `exports` map**, and in all three the permissive answer is the one a developer sees first.

## What it cost, and what the repair coupled

PR #8668's `Bundle Analysis` red was **not a bundle problem at all** — the job never reached the bundle (`BUDGET_STEP_OUTCOME: skipped`, comment kind `not-measured`). ⚠️ A PM hypothesis that it was the `i18n-locales` ceiling was offered as a lead and **falsified**; a dev who had taken it as fact would have hunted for bytes in a job that weighed none.

The repair imported the workspace sources the aliases already resolved to (identical modules at runtime) and added `node` to `apps/console/tsconfig.json`'s `types` for a `typeof process` guard in the app-shell source that pulls in. **Two alternatives were rejected, and the reasons are the useful part:**

- ⛔ **publish the six bindings from the barrels** — permanently widens two packages' public API, and would publish **`__resetInboxArrivals`, a declared test seam**, so a dev-only fixture could pretend to be a consumer;
- ⛔ **`tsconfig` `paths` mapping the subpaths to dist** — teaches that `@object-ui/app-shell/hooks/x` **is** importable when it is not, i.e. plants exactly the false premise this card is about.

⇒ the shipped arm is the only one leaving both packages' published contracts byte-identical. ⚠️ **But it has a declared cost**: `node` in the console's `types` pulls **30 workspace source files** (27 app-shell, 3 auth, of 3712) into the console's type program, so **an app-shell source error can now surface as a console build failure.** Recorded here rather than left in a PR comment.

## Directions, sketched without recommending — this is a triage call

- **A — make the alias agree with the contract.** Have the dev-server aliases resolve only what the `exports` maps publish, so a fixture cannot import what a consumer cannot. ⚠️ Likely to break other fixtures that already depend on the permissive behaviour — **measure the population before choosing**.
- **B — a gate.** Something that type-checks the dev-only fixtures the way `Build Console` does, so the divergence is caught where it is written rather than in CI's build step. ⚠️ Note the existing gates did **not** catch this: the fixture is not in a published package and no test imports it.
- **C — leave the mechanism, remove the coupling.** Keep the alias as-is, and undo the `types: ["node"]` widening by other means once a better arm exists.
- **D — nothing.** The `exports` maps are the contract, CI caught it, and the cost was one build failure.

⚠️ **A and B are not alternatives** — A stops the divergence being writable; B stops it reaching CI. Either alone leaves the other half.

## Related

objectui#8691 (test type-checking runs at two different `lib` levels per package — the same *"green under one tool, red under another"* family, different axis) · objectui#3378 (the guard for the `--filter` vitest spelling) · objectui#8592 (`eslint .` walking git-ignored build output — a fourth tool disagreeing about which files are in scope) · PR #8668 (where this was measured)

## Dedup

⚠️ **Declared, NOT claimed.** This repo's `search_issues` returns **false zeros** — measured repeatedly, including `total_count: 0` for a token carried in a matching issue's own title — and last night the **REST search endpoint answered 403 on three queries including its control**. ⇒ no zero from either channel is evidence of absence. Manual check performed instead: the devx/tooling findings filed since 2026-09-07 were read by title. objectui#8691 is the nearest neighbour and is a **different axis** (compiler `lib` level, not module resolution). Nothing found on Vite alias prefix matching.
